title.narrative: Strengthening integrated service delivery for returnees, nomadic and host communities in Nangarhar, Maidan Wardak and Balkh provinces

description.narrative: The overal objective is to Promote peaceful, inclusive, stable, and resilient target communities by enhancing social cohesion among and between returnees, nomadic (Kuchi), and host communities through an integrated multi-sectoral approach.Outcome 1: Increased equitable use of natural resources and basic services, thereby reducing social tension and conflict over resources and inequitable access to services between nomadic (Kuchi), returnees, and host communities.Outcome 2: Strengthened economic and social resilience, leading to increased perceptions of social cohesion, durable engagement, and meaningful participation of targeted host, returnee, and Kuchi communities, especially marginalized children, in decision-making processes.

This 24-month programme will directly reach 102,400 people (27,597girls, 28,723 boys, 22,579women and 23,501men) including an estimated 10,240 persons with disabilities, across districts in Balkh, Nangarhar and Maidan Wardak provinces. The proposed integrated approach means that beneficiaries reached under each output will overlap 100%. The number of men and boys, and women and girls are estimated based on population data, and the impact of societal norms, meaning that for women and girls, their access to services is most often determined by their male relatives and spouses

With a focus on promoting social cohesion and preventing future conflicts, the project aims to address basic needs at the community level, while enhancing community engagement and improving the availability and equitable access to resources across H&N, FSL, CP, WASH and psychosocial wellbeing. Through collaboration with national and sub-national stakeholders and through partnership with local organisation The Liaison Office (TLO), the project will strengthen systems and provide sustainable solutions to meet the basic needs of the targeted returnee, nomadic (Kuchi) and host communities, employing conflict-sensitive approaches.
